anti_overlap: fd-compute-module-architecture covers the Rust module structure and tick pipeline integration point
fd-compute-supply-chain-realism covers whether field values and calibration match real-world semiconductor economics
fd-compute-signal-consumer-contracts covers how state fields are read by consumer modules
decision_lens: Flag state designs where a country's role in the semiconductor ecosystem cannot be expressed without a code change — if TWN and USA differ only in field values, the schema is extensible; if they require different struct variants, that is a design smell.
focus: Whether per-country and per-region compute state is structured to support the heterogeneous distribution of semiconductor infrastructure — fab countries, consumer countries, equipment countries, and sanctioned countries all need distinct state shapes
name: fd-compute-regional-state-tracking
persona: A data modeler who designed per-entity state for large-scale agent simulations. Focuses on whether the state schema can express the full range of real-world country configurations without encoding special cases as magic constants or missing data.
review_areas: Verify ComputeCountryState (or equivalent) has fields for all roles: fab_capacity_nm7_wafers_per_month (producer), gpu_stockpile_units (consumer/military), data_center_capacity_gw (cloud/AI), equipment_export_license_tier (equipment supplier like NLD), and entity_list_membership (sanctioned receiver) — confirm no role requires a separate struct

Check that advanced-node fab capacity is tracked at the node-size level (3nm, 5nm, 7nm, 28nm separately) rather than as a single capacity scalar — a country like CHN with mature-node capacity but no advanced-node capacity must be distinguishable from TWN without field overlap

Assess water and energy as local constraints on data center scaling: data_center_capacity_gw should be bounded by regional energy_grid_headroom and water_stress_index — verify these are read from existing country-level fields (if they exist) rather than being hard-coded per-country constants

Verify the export control state is per-directed-pair, not per-country: USA can export to KOR but not CHN; NLD can export to TWN but is sanctioned for certain node sizes to CHN — confirm the data structure supports (exporter, importer, control_tier) triples, not just (country, control_tier) pairs

Check that compute state participates in the save/restore cycle: ComputeCountryState must be serde-serializable, included in the simulation snapshot, and correctly restored in from_snapshot() so that a saved game with a compute advantage correctly restores that advantage

Evaluate GPU/TPU allocation tracking: if a country's gpu_stockpile is consumed by both military AI and civilian AI workloads, verify there is an allocation record (not just a total) so players and agents can observe the competition for scarce units and deployment actions can target specific allocations
success_hints: A country with no advanced fab capacity, no equipment export role, and entity-list sanctioned status can be fully described by ComputeCountryState field values alone — no code branch special-cases it
Saving and restoring a simulation at tick N with CHN on the entity list and TWN at 40% fab capacity produces identical compute pressure outputs at tick N+1 as the unsaved simulation would
task_context: Shadow Work tracks per-country state in PressureStore (HashMap<String, CountryPressures>) and SupplyChainPhysicalEconomy (flat Vec indexed by country_index). The compute module must model heterogeneous country roles: Taiwan (fab), Netherlands (equipment), USA (consumer + sanctions authority), China (consumer + sanctioned), South Korea (fab + consumer). State must be serializable for save/restore via SimulationTicker::default() replacement.
